title: Finite-Sample Coverage Bounds for Score-Tail Trimmed ATE Inference with Learned Boundary Propensity
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the learned-propensity score-tail coverage graph, including the moment-bound interface, and the final typed math and decision referees passed without findings. The delivered result gives conservative uniform Gaussian and Wald coverage bounds with polynomial tuning over the specialized fixed-floor class. The field floor was missed because the rate is not sharp, the stated minimax criterion is degenerate, and the projected paper score caps the achieved tier at incremental; a variance-controlled procedure with a matching lower bound would require a new theorem program.
tldr: Weak overlap makes the full-population IPW score heavy tailed, while a learned boundary propensity perturbs pooled absolute-score ranks, signed tail correction, and studentization. For every explicit admissible deterministic tuning triple, the note proves the uniform finite-sample bound \(\Delta_N\le K\bar{\mathfrak E}_N\) and honest Wald coverage for the original ATE, allowing endpoint atoms. Every fixed nonempty class in the declared smoothness region now has a conservative explicit polynomial schedule with error \(O\{N^{-a/8}(\log N)^{1/8}\}\), where the positive exponent \(a\) is displayed in the general-rate proposition. On the \(\gamma=2\), \(\beta=4\), \(\eta=1\) benchmark, a sharper parameter-specific balance yields \(O\{N^{-1/110}(\log N)^{7/44}\}\). The unrestricted studentizer minimax criterion is exponentially degenerate, so it remains only a negative diagnostic; a variance-consistent or interval-length-controlled frontier remains open.
gap: ChaudhuriHill2025 proves asymptotic Gaussian inference for corrected score-tail trimming, and the banked scalar boundary-propensity proposal supplies the class witness, primitive score tails, boundary learner, and qualitative Wald limit. Neither gives a finite-sample coverage-error envelope that jointly tracks propensity learning, pooled rank transfer, two signed intermediate orders, a random realized cutoff, and empirical studentization.
fill: The project treats the reused tail and likelihood lemmas as inputs, proves quantitative random-cutoff and studentizer bounds, combines them with a truncated-score Gaussian approximation, and delivers the joint Kolmogorov and Wald coverage-error envelope \(\bar{\mathfrak E}_N\) together with the \(\gamma=2\), \(\beta=4\) early-kill rate.
